requirements.R-ABORT-RO: start-up aborts before ANY write to the store: every input file byte-identical after the attempt (sha256 equal), no rename, no .bak rotation, no settings write; the refusal is reported out-of-band (process exit code + boot incident log outside the store)
requirements.R-NO-MANAGE: no AccountContext is created for the account: no order, cancel, stop repair, reconcile booking or journal write is issued; protective orders already on the exchange are left untouched
requirements.R-EVIDENCE: the damaged bytes are preserved bit-for-bit (copy-then-mark, never move-then-rewrite) and linked from a durable incident record that survives restarts
requirements.R-DURABLE-FAIL: the failed-closed condition is itself durable: a restart (with or without intervening saves) returns to the same blocked state until an explicit reconciliation record exists
requirements.R-RECON-GATE: management (and every new-risk path, MANUAL included) stays blocked until a reconciliation record binds state generation G to an exchange snapshot that matches it (positions, open orders, protective orders) or the owner adopts/flattens each difference explicitly; resuming entries alone never clears it
requirements.R-NO-EMPTY: an initialized account (marker or any store generation or evidence present) can never load as an empty portfolio; an empty portfolio is only legal for a first run whose exchange snapshot is flat (no positions, no open orders) or after an explicit owner adoption record
requirements.R-BACKUP-CANDIDATE: an older generation (backup) is offered as a reconciliation CANDIDATE, never silently promoted to managed state; it becomes managed only after R-RECON-GATE passes against the exchange
requirements.R-FIRST-RUN-FLAT: first-run initialization requires a successful exchange snapshot; a non-flat account blocks initialization until the owner adopts or closes each position/order explicitly
requirements.R-GEN-MONOTONIC: every store write carries (generation, writer_build, format_version, min_reader_version); a reader that sees a generation written by a newer build, or a lower generation than the highest it has seen (rollback/stale copy), aborts read-only (R-ABORT-RO)
requirements.R-SINGLE-SOURCE: the account marker, the store and its backups are one versioned unit: one invalid member blocks the unit; a backup can never silently clear an owner-confirmation requirement
requirements.R-STRICT-PARSE: the store parser treats as DAMAGE (rule 4, HOLD with evidence) - never as a valid document and never as an uncaught exception: duplicate object keys, NaN/Infinity tokens, numbers outside the declared range (quantities above the venue maximum, integers outside int64), any bytes after the document (NUL padding included), and a document that is all NUL
requirements.R-VERSION-TYPE: a format/version header that is not a JSON integer >= 0 (string, float, bool, null, negative) is an UNKNOWN format and is handled like a future one (rule 1, ABORT-RO): the reader cannot prove it is older
requirements.R-WRITE-VALIDATES: every record is validated with the reader schema BEFORE commit; a record the reader would reject is never committed (the intent is refused and nothing is sent)
requirements.R-INTENT-SHAPE: an order intent carries kind, client id, created_ms (integer UTC ms) and a quantity that is > 0, a whole number of venue steps and <= the venue maximum; any other shape is refused at write time and is damage at read time
requirements.R-NOTFOUND-NOT-PROOF: a bare not-found order lookup never resolves an intent; only a final order record (or a venue error that proves rejection) does. Until then the outcome is unknown (None) and the symbol/side stays HOLD for new risk
requirements.R-RESULT-BEFORE-APPLY: ownership changes only from a durable result record; reconcile never books an exit (stop, resync, close) at a guessed price from a position delta; an unexplained delta is a HOLD item
requirements.R-UNCOMMITTED: files that are not part of a committed generation (temp, partial, orphan) are never read as state and never silently deleted; they are reported and kept as evidence. A torn uncommitted temp alone does not block MANAGE
requirements.R-IO-FAULT: an I/O fault on the store (ENOSPC, EROFS, a directory or other non-file at a store path, permission) means no intent can be made durable, so nothing is sent; it is reported out-of-band; no partial generation and no partial evidence is left behind
requirements.R-KNOWN-EMPTY: an empty portfolio is KNOWN empty only after a proven first run with a flat exchange, or through a journaled chain of results from the last non-empty generation; otherwise ownership is unknown (None, never []) and can never auto-match a flat exchange
requirements.R-IDENTITY: account binding is verified before any match; position equality never proves identity; an identity mismatch stays HOLD until the owner confirms the binding AND a fresh reconciliation record exists
requirements.R-MATCH: "match" = same account binding + snapshot younger than the max age + per symbol/side aggregate quantity equal within the venue step tolerance + every owned order/stop id present with the expected lifecycle state + no unowned position or order; re-checked atomically at promotion
requirements.R-NO-AUTO-CANCEL-FOREIGN: an unknown/foreign order or position is never cancelled, closed or adopted automatically; it is a per-item owner decision while the account is HOLD
requirements.R-ROLLBACK-DETECT: a readable generation lower than the high-water (or than what the exchange history proves) is HOLD, never MANAGE; with no surviving high-water, the exchange difference alone must still yield HOLD
requirements.R-HOLD: HOLD (Codex rulings 3 and 6): no new risk from any source (auto, manual, Telegram, UI, grid, maker); non-protective open intents are cancelled or drained through the priority queue; a late or partial fill is adopted and protected and stays blocked from new risk until reconciled; protective orders are kept; durable local append-only intent/result/incident events are allowed; no promotion and no reconciliation claim
requirements.R-NO-LEGACY-IMPORT: NEWCORE never reads legacy state/settings/install files as state (Codex ruling 10): their presence is reported, their bytes stay identical, and NEWCORE starts with INIT on testnet (flat exchange -> MANAGE empty; non-flat -> HOLD-INIT)
